headline: Mile High slipped to 24-28; Arrowhead is a 9.5-point reply

sectionTitles.currentState: West lead gone, deadline week open
sectionTitles.pressConferences: Reid on Monday after the 28-24 loss

dek: Kansas City is 5-2 after Denver closed a 24-28 divisional loss with two fourth-quarter touchdowns, and the next kickoff is home against the Jets on Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM CT on CBS with the Chiefs laying 9.5.
videoHook: Denver took the lead back at Q4 1:56, and the next assignment is a 9.5-point home number against the Jets.
theEdge: ESPN FPI lists Kansas City at 80.3 percent to beat the Jets, and DraftKings has the Chiefs minus 9.5 on a 46.5 total — a home price that still has to live with 10 quarterback hits and a fourth-quarter lead that finished 24-28.
editorNotes: Last-game window is afternoon; do not use night. KC possession 31:29, DEN 28:31. Mahomes 10 QB hits, KC recorded 2. Seattle prior box stays separate: KC 213 yards, 24:09. Scorers on made TDs/FGs are unknown except Coleman’s Q4 5-yard rush TD and Butker’s missed 54. Zone-blitz card is a Jets call only.

pressConferences.title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes & Chris Jones Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 8

storyline.lede: Kansas City put 399 yards and 22 first downs on Denver and still walked out of Empower Field on the wrong side of 24-28. Patrick Mahomes was sharp enough to throw three touchdowns, Kenneth Walker III touched the ball 25 times, and the defense held Bo Nix’s offense to 2-of-11 on third down — then the fourth quarter took the AFC West lead with it.
body: The scoreboard path is the film. Denver’s 39-yard field goal at Q1 9:43 made it 0-3.

Denver scored a 2-yard touchdown at Q4 8:55 to make it 24-21. Butker’s 54-yard try at Q4 2:36 was wide right. Jonah Coleman then ran up the middle for a 5-yard touchdown at Q4 1:56, and the extra point made it 24-28. Kansas City’s last series reached the 1 and ended on downs at Q4 0:00. Andy Reid, on Monday, called the loss self-inflicted, and Arrowhead Pride framed the finish as a fourth-and-goal stop.

The slate now says 5-2, Denver is 6-2, and Arrowhead Pride has Kansas City in the wild-card mix with Buffalo at 6-1 atop the AFC. The next kickoff is not a referendum on the whole season. It is Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM CT, CBS, at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium, against the Jets, with DraftKings listing Kansas City minus 9.5 on a 46.5 total and ESPN FPI at 80.3 percent.

lastGameReview.label: Week 8 · Sun, Nov 1 · 3:25 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Empower Field, Kansas City led 24-13 after a 4-yard touchdown at Q3 1:38 and lost 24-28 when Denver scored at Q4 8:55 and again at Q4 1:56. Both teams finished with 11 drives and zero turnovers. Kansas City had 22 first downs, 6-of-14 on third down, 90 rushing yards on 24 attempts, 309 net passing yards, 399 total yards, and 31:29 of possession. Denver had 21 first downs, 2-of-11 on third down, 77 rushing yards on 23 attempts, 217 net passing yards, 294 total yards, and 28:31 of possession.

analysis.body: Mahomes finished 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns, with two sacks and a 120.1 rating. Denver recorded 10 quarterback hits on him. Kansas City recorded 2 quarterback hits. George Karlaftis had the sack on Nix, and on that play Karlaftis forced a fumble that Adam Trautman recovered for Denver. Nix was 20-of-32 with one sack and a 103.9 rating. The explosive throws in the wire included Courtland Sutton for 23 on a deep left and Jaylen Waddle for 35 on a deep middle.

Walker carried 21 times for 69 yards and added 4 catches, 25 touches in all. The team rush total was still 90, so the other three carries — Emmett Johnson once, Mahomes twice — had to supply the rest. Johnson also caught 5 passes for 128 yards and a touchdown, 6 touches with that one rush. Rashee Rice caught 7, Travis Kelce 5, Xavier Worthy 3. The 73-yard touchdown at Q2 7:40 is the explosive score on the sheet; the scoring table does not name the receiver. All one Kansas City touchdowns were throws: 11, 73, and 4 yards.

Denver’s late rush tape is the part that traveled. Marvin Mims Jr. ran right end for 14 yards to the Kansas City 4 at Q4 10:56. Coleman, 11 rushes and 4 catches for 15 touches, scored the 5-yard touchdown up the middle at Q4 1:56. The 1-yard and 2-yard Denver touchdowns stay unassigned. Kansas City’s answering series after that score shows Walker right end to the Denver 12, right end to the 1, and up the middle for no gain at the 1 before the turnover on downs.

Flags and the missed kick sit next to the yardage. Kristian Fulton was flagged for defensive pass interference and an illegal block above the waist. Drue Tranquill and Alohi Gilman had wiped plays on a face mask and a defensive pass interference. Trey Smith’s holding erased a Walker right-end gain. Gilman’s unnecessary roughness came at Q4 11:23. J. Moore’s false start at Q4 0:04 wiped a play. Butker was good from 45 in the second quarter and wide right from 54 at Q4 2:36, with the score 24-21. Hunter Nourzad reported eligible on one snap, Q4 15:00, a Walker carry up the middle for 1 yard. Denver’s Alex Palczewski reported eligible on several snaps, including Nix’s right-end run for no gain at the 1.

takeaways.title: The yardage won the middle, not the finish
takeaways.body: 399 yards, 22 first downs, and 31:29 of possession produced 24 points and a loss. Denver scored 28 on 294 yards, including two fourth-quarter touchdowns after trailing 24-13.

takeaways.title: Mahomes’ line and the hit count are different facts
takeaways.body: He was 30-of-41 for 321 yards, three touchdowns, two sacks, and a 120.1 rating. Denver still put 10 quarterback hits on him. Kansas City’s own quarterback-hit total was 2.

takeaways.title: The last series died at the 1
takeaways.body: After Coleman’s 5-yard touchdown made it 24-28, Walker’s carries reached the Denver 1 and the drive ended on downs at Q4 0:00. Butker had already missed from 54 at Q4 2:36.

whatWorked: Mahomes’ 30-of-41, 321-yard, three-touchdown line and a 120.1 rating.
Johnson’s 5 catches for 128 yards and a touchdown, plus Rice’s 7 catches and Kelce’s 5.
Third-down defense: Denver was 2-of-11, and Karlaftis recorded the sack and forced the fumble Trautman recovered.
Zero Kansas City turnovers across 11 drives, with 6-of-14 on third down.
whatDidnt: 10 quarterback hits and two sacks on Mahomes, against 90 team rushing yards.
Butker’s 54-yard miss, wide right, at Q4 2:36.
A stack of Kansas City penalties, including two on Fulton and two on Gilman, plus the final downs at the 1.

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 5-2 after a second straight loss, and the AFC West lead that came with the 5-0 start is now Denver’s. Arrowhead Pride’s Week 9 roundup has national rankings sliding — ESPN from 4 to 6 — while the same building is arguing trade deadline, tackle rotation, and how a 399-yard afternoon still lost.

workOn.title: Finish a lead that is already on the board
workOn.body: The 24-13 margin after Q3 1:38 asked the offense to stay on schedule and the defense to keep Denver out of the low red area. Three Denver touchdowns and a missed 54 flipped it. Against the Jets, script the first third down after a score, not only the first snap of the game.

workOn.title: Protection that survives 10 hits
workOn.body: Mahomes took two sacks and 10 quarterback hits. Mike Caliendo started for Kingsley Suamataia; Reid said Monday the change was not a disciplinary benching. The Jets game plan has to give Walker and Johnson easy pictures so 30-plus throws are not the only way to 24 points.

workOn.title: Early-down rush that matches the touch count
workOn.body: Walker’s 21 carries produced 69 yards. The team rushed for 90 on 24 attempts. That is a volume plan without a downhill average. Inside zone on first down is the install, not another 21-carry grind that still leaves third-and-long.

thinkAbout.title: Is the receiver market a real deadline or a loud week?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict has tied the final series in Denver to a wide-receiver trade case, and another piece floats Jerry Jeudy if Cleveland cooperates. Rice had 7 catches, Johnson 128 yards, Kelce 5 grabs, Worthy 3. The staff should separate a thin explosive group from a finish that failed at the 1.

thinkAbout.title: How hard should Brett Veach push?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict argues Veach cannot sit on picks in Mahomes’ prime, and a separate note says this Jets week is a chance to scout trade targets in person. Weigh that against a defense that held Denver to 294 yards and 2-of-11 on third down and still lost the quarter that mattered.

thinkAbout.title: Where does the West math sit?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict’s power rankings say the division lead is gone. Arrowhead Pride’s playoff picture puts Kansas City in the wild-card mix, with Buffalo 6-1 and Denver among the teams in front. A home win on Sun Nov 8 does not restore the West by itself. It stops a two-game slide before Atlanta.

gamePlan.lede: The assignment is the Jets at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on Sun Nov 8, 12:00 PM CT, CBS. Kansas City is a 9.5-point favorite on a 46.5 total, and ESPN FPI has the Chiefs at 80.3 percent. The number assumes the 399-yard Denver tape shows up without the fourth-quarter leak.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City’s offense can stress width and depth: Mahomes at 30-of-41, Johnson as the explosive catcher, Rice and Kelce as the volume targets, Walker as the 25-touch back. The liability is the rush average and the 10 hits. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense just held an opponent to 2-of-11 on third down and 294 yards and still allowed 28 points, so the Jets plan is explosives first, then rally tackles, not a hope that third-and-long saves a lead by itself. Eric Bieniemy has to marry Walker’s inside zone to quick answers so Mahomes is not throwing 41 times into a heavy rush again.

keys.title: Score the first red-zone trip and the one after halftime
keys.body: Against the Jets, take the 11-yard and 4-yard touchdown answers from the Denver tape and make them the scripted red-zone calls, with Kelce and Rice as the primary reads.

keys.title: Give Walker a first-down identity, then the screen
keys.body: 21 carries for 69 yards will not beat a stacked box if the Jets sell out on Mahomes. Inside zone on early downs, then a screen to Walker or Johnson when the rush shows the same heat that produced 10 hits.

keys.title: Two-deep on explosives, heat on second-and-medium
keys.body: Sutton’s 23-yard deep left and Waddle’s 35-yard deep middle were the Denver verticals. Cover-2 takes the top off similar shots. The zone blitz is the change-up on second down so the Jets cannot sit in a clean dropback.

script: Open in 11 personnel with Walker inside zone, Rice and Kelce as the play-action-boot and mesh answers if the Jets spin to man.
On the first third-and-medium, throw the spacing screen to Walker before asking Mahomes to hold a seven-step drop.
If Johnson wins a seam, come back to four verticals once, with Worthy outside and Kelce bending to the hash.
After any Kansas City score, call Cover-2 on the first two Jets snaps and rally the alley.
Use one simulated pressure on second-and-6 or longer, with Karlaftis as the featured rusher and a second-level drop behind him.
In the low red area, prefer Kelce or Rice on the 4-yard and 11-yard pictures from Denver over a 54-yard field-goal conversation.

spotlight.title: 24-13 was the lead that left
spotlight.body: Denver’s 2-yard touchdown at Q4 8:55 and Coleman’s 5-yard touchdown at Q4 1:56 made it 24-28. That is the sequence the Jets week has to answer.

spotlight.title: Johnson’s 128 next to Rice’s 7
spotlight.body: Emmett Johnson caught 5 passes for 128 yards and a touchdown. Rashee Rice caught 7, Kelce 5, Worthy 3. The skill group produced; the last series still died at the Denver 1.

spotlight.title: Caliendo in, Suamataia out of the start
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride reported Mike Caliendo filled in for Kingsley Suamataia, and Reid said the move was not disciplinary. Ten quarterback hits make that rotation a Week 9 story, not a one-game footnote.

spotlight.title: 80.3 percent is not a coronation
spotlight.body: ESPN FPI has Kansas City at 80.3 percent against the Jets and the opponent at 19.6 percent. DraftKings has the Chiefs minus 9.5 on 46.5. The Denver loss was a one-score game with zero turnovers. Treat the home number as a standard, not a result.

matchups.unit: Mahomes and the protection vs. the Jets rush
matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, Mike Caliendo, the starting line Reid used in Denver
matchups.opponent: Jets pass rush, unspecified in the wire
matchups.note: Mahomes was 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns at 120.1, with two sacks. Denver recorded 10 quarterback hits. Until the Jets show their rush plan, the edge is the hit count, not the completion line.

matchups.unit: Walker and inside zone vs. the Jets front
matchups.note: Walker had 21 carries for 69 yards and 4 catches. Team rushing was 90 on 24 attempts. Volume is a Chiefs edge if Bieniemy steals early downs; the 3-plus yard average is the caution.

matchups.unit: Rice, Kelce, Johnson vs. Jets coverage
matchups.chiefs: Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, Emmett Johnson, Xavier Worthy
matchups.note: Johnson’s 128 yards and a touchdown, Rice’s 7 catches, and Kelce’s 5 catches are the clearest skill edge on the sheet. Worthy’s 3 catches keep the outside honest.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo’s third-down shell vs. the Jets offense
matchups.chiefs: Steve Spagnuolo, George Karlaftis, Nick Bolton
matchups.note: Denver was 2-of-11 on third down and gained 294 yards, with Nix at 20-of-32. Kansas City recorded 2 quarterback hits and Karlaftis had the sack. That down-and-distance profile is the edge to carry home, if explosives stay in front of the safeties.

matchups.unit: Late-game points vs. a one-score finish
matchups.chiefs: Harrison Butker and the fourth-quarter offense
matchups.opponent: Any opponent that can score twice after trailing by 11
matchups.note: Butker made a 45-yard field goal at Q2 0:19 and missed a 54-yarder wide right at Q4 2:36. Denver then scored the 5-yard touchdown. The Jets do not need a special-teams miracle if Kansas City protects a lead the way it did at Mile High.

xsandos.title: Walker inside zone on first down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 at home against the Jets, before Denver’s 10-hit rush picture becomes the down-and-distance.
xsandos.why: Walker carried 21 times for 69 and the team rushed for 90.
xsandos.coaching: Walker, press the play-side A-gap path the Denver tape already showed up the middle, one cut, and fall forward. Mahomes carries the keep only if the end widens; his two scrambles in Denver were answers, not the plan.

xsandos.title: Walker screen against the heat
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-8 or 3rd-and-6 after a Jets rush shows four or more, the down Denver turned into 10 quarterback hits and two sacks.
xsandos.why: Mahomes was 30-of-41 and still absorbed 10 hits. A screen to Walker or Johnson lets the line climb and gives Rice a clearout so the rush does not get a free run at a 9.5-point favorite.
xsandos.coaching: Walker, sell the inside zone step, then slide to the screen. Johnson is the alternate if the Jets squeeze the back. Mahomes, throw on time; do not drift into the 10-hit pocket.

xsandos.title: Rice-Kelce mesh vs. man
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 in Jets territory, the down Kansas City converted often enough to reach 6-of-14 and still needs in the red area.
xsandos.why: Rice caught 7 and Kelce 5 in Denver. A rub between those two, with Worthy sitting and Johnson as the late cross, is the man-beater that does not require a 73-yard explosive to move the chains.
xsandos.coaching: Rice and Kelce, cross at five yards and do not drift into the same landmark. Worthy, sit if the corner sinks. Mahomes, throw the first open window; Cyrus Allen is the fourth option, not the first read.

xsandos.title: Four verticals once Johnson has won a seam
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-4 or after a Jets safety rotation, the look Denver could not always squeeze when Johnson finished with 128 yards.
xsandos.why: Johnson’s 5-for-128 and a touchdown say the vertical answer is already on the roster. Worthy and Rice stretch the corners; Kelce bends to the hash. One shot is enough if the Jets spin late.
xsandos.coaching: Johnson, take the seam and bend to the near hash. Worthy, stay on top of the corner the way the incomplete deep right to him in Denver still occupied Patrick Surtain. Mahomes, throw the hash if the middle closes.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 after a Kansas City score
xsandos.situation: First three Jets snaps after a Chiefs touchdown or field goal, the moment Denver answered a 24-13 lead with points.
xsandos.why: Sutton’s 23-yard deep left and Waddle’s 35-yard deep middle were the explosives in a game Denver won with 294 yards. Two deep, five under takes that shot away and lets the alley rally, which is what a 9.5-point home favorite needs after it scores.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo, call the shell before the Jets can check to a shot. Safeties, stay square. Bolton and the linebackers, rally the flat so a Coleman-style dump-off does not become a 15-touch problem. Karlaftis, rush contain, do not vacate the edge.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz on second-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7 against the Jets, a call Spagnuolo can steal once the offense has shown max protection.
xsandos.why: Kansas City recorded only 2 quarterback hits in Denver while Nix was 20-of-32. A simulated pressure — show four, drop a lineman, rush a second-level player — is the change-up that keeps a clean dropback from becoming another 103.9-rating afternoon for the other quarterback.
xsandos.coaching: Karlaftis, win the edge on the rush. The dropped lineman has to get to the hook so the show does not become a vacant lane. Bolton, time the second-level rush. Spagnuolo, use it as a down-stealer, then return to Cover-2.

coaching.detail: On Monday, Reid pointed at self-inflicted issues after the 28-24 loss. The penalty sheet — Fulton twice, Gilman twice, Smith’s holding, Kelce’s false start, Moore’s late false start — is the list the meeting should start with.
Mahomes was efficient at 30-of-41 and three touchdowns, and the team still rushed for 90. Bieniemy’s Jets script has to cash Walker earlier so the 73-yard touchdown is a bonus, not the requirement.

coaching.topic: Spagnuolo and a 2-of-11 that still lost
coaching.detail: Denver was 2-of-11 on third down and held the ball 28:31. The points came anyway, including Coleman’s 5-yard touchdown. The Jets plan is explosives and the low red area, not another third-down percentage that hides a 24-28.

personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride reported a last-second offensive line change, with Mike Caliendo in for Kingsley Suamataia. Reid said the decision was not disciplinary. Ten quarterback hits make the next start a protection question.

Arrowhead Pride’s snap-count piece flags Cyrus Allen for a season-high workload in the 28-24 loss. He finished with 2 catches. He is a viable fourth receiver in the Jets mesh and vertical cards, not a volume replacement for Rice.
Hunter Nourzad reported eligible at Q4 15:00 on a Walker carry up the middle for 1 yard. That is one snap on the list, a short-yardage look, not a new base offense.

strategies: Steal first down with Walker inside zone so 6-of-14 on third down is not the offense’s identity again.
Answer heat with the screen before Mahomes absorbs another 10-hit pocket.
Use Rice and Kelce on mesh in man looks; Johnson is the explosive, not the every-down crosser.
Call Cover-2 immediately after Kansas City scores.
Steal one second-and-medium with a zone blitz, Karlaftis on the edge, then get back to two-deep.
In the low red area, throw the 4-yard and 11-yard pictures before the conversation becomes a 54-yard field goal.
debates: Does a 399-yard, zero-turnover loss say the skill group is fine, or does the final series at the 1 still justify a receiver call before the deadline?
Should Caliendo keep the start, or does Suamataia return once the staff separates a lineup change from the 10 hits?
Is Spagnuolo’s 2-of-11 third-down game a defensive win that the fourth quarter stole, or a red-area failure?
Arrowhead Addict has floated moving on from Reid. Is that a real staff question at 5-2, or a loud reaction to one 24-28 finish?
Does laying 9.5 at home on Sun Nov 8 paper over a two-game slide, or is 80.3 percent the right read if the Jets cannot match Denver’s fourth quarter?
